title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery: Advanced review set explorer for KQL queries
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap record, Microsoft's tenant notice and Microsoft Learn. Its access controls, audit-search instructions and licensing explanation are accurate, and it distinguishes the documented preview from the planned general availability rollout.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Advanced Review Set Explorer is a new tab in review sets in Microsoft Purview eDiscovery (Premium).
claims.quote: We're introducing the Advanced Review Set Explorer (public preview) for review sets in Microsoft Purview eDiscovery (Premium).

claims.claim: Reviewers use Kusto Query Language (KQL) in the explorer.
claims.quote: lets reviewers run real-time big data analytics on review set content by using a defined subset of Kusto Query Language (KQL).

claims.claim: The roadmap describes complex filtering of review set data.
claims.quote: Reviewers can utilize powerful Kusto query constructs like complex filtering, pattern-based text extraction, and data format parsing

claims.claim: The explorer supports aggregation of review set data.
claims.quote: The `summarize` operator aggregates data by applying functions like `count()`, `sum()`, or `avg()`, and groups results based on specified columns.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The explorer supports pattern-based text extraction.
claims.quote: Build powerful queries with complex filtering, pattern-based text extraction, and data format parsing.

claims.claim: Explorer query results can be displayed as a table or chart.
claims.quote: Queries run against the full set of indexed items and return either tabular results or chart visualizations.

claims.claim: The explorer opens at Microsoft Purview portal > eDiscovery > Cases > case > Review sets > review set > Advanced review set explorer (preview).
claims.quote:
Select the **eDiscovery** solution card, and then select **Cases** in the left navigation.
3. Select a case, and then select the **Review sets** tab.
4. Select a review set, and then select the **Advanced review set explorer (preview)** tab.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Explorer queries are read-only and do not modify review set content.
claims.quote: Queries are read-only and don't modify review set content.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The explorer queries the current review set's indexed items rather than introducing a new data source.
claims.quote: All queries in the Advanced review set explorer (preview) run against the current review set's indexed items. You don't need to specify a table name. The review set acts as the default data source.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A query returning more than 10,000 results returns only the first 10,000.
claims.quote: If the query returns more than 10,000 results, it returns only the first 10,000 results. Modify the query to narrow down the results.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The explorer does not support all Kusto operators and properties.
claims.quote: The Advanced review set explorer (preview) doesn't support all Kusto operators and properties.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Older review sets may lack properties and return column-not-found errors.
claims.quote: Some older review sets might not support certain KQL properties if those properties weren't available when the review set was created and data was generated. Querying an unsupported property in an older review set results in a column not found error.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft's remedy for unsupported properties in older review sets is to create a new review set and regenerate data using Add to review set.
claims.quote: To resolve this error, create a new review set and use the **Add to review set** process to regenerate the data with the latest supported properties.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The notice names no explorer-only admin setting, and a tenant or case switch to disable it remains undocumented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Advanced review set explorer" "disable" "settings". Read MC1221453 and edisc-review-set-explorer; search excerpts for edisc-review-set-manage and edisc-settings-review-sets document other settings, not an explorer switch.

claims.claim: KQL provides more sophisticated slicing and aggregation than the existing search and filtering experience.
claims.quote: power users and advanced reviewers often need greater flexibility to slice, aggregate, and analyze review set data in more sophisticated ways. To meet this need, we're adding a Kusto Query Language (KQL)-based experience

claims.claim: Learn supplies an explorer example listing external recipient addresses per item.
claims.quote: Find all review set items that include at least one external recipient (outside your organization contoso.com), and list those external email addresses for each item.

claims.claim: The feature page describes no autonomous explorer actions.
claims.quote: Searched: "Advanced review set explorer" disable license pricing audit KQL; read edisc-review-set-explorer in full. It describes reviewers writing and running read-only queries and no autonomous execution mechanism.

claims.claim: Adding data to a review set may change later query results.
claims.quote: Results reflect the current indexed state of the review set. If you add more data to the review set, the query might return different results.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes
claims.claim: To analyse a user's data with premium eDiscovery features enabled, the user needs Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5, subject to the stated add-on alternative.
claims.quote: To analyze a user's data when premium eDiscovery features are enabled, the user must be assigned an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes
claims.claim: Office 365 E1 or Office 365 or Microsoft 365 E3 users can instead receive the Microsoft Purview Suite or Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit add-on.
claims.quote: Alternatively, users with an Office 365 E1 or an Office 365 or Microsoft 365 E3 license can be assigned a Microsoft Purview Suite (formerly known as Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance) or Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit add-on license.

claims.claim: Administrators, compliance officers and legal personnel assigned as case members do not need an E5 licence to collect, view and analyse data with premium features.
claims.quote: Administrators, compliance officers, or legal personnel who are assigned to cases as members and use premium eDiscovery features to collect, view, and analyze data don't need an E5 license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The explorer is included within the existing eDiscovery premium licensing framework rather than having a published separate entitlement.
claims.quote: To analyze a user's data when premium eDiscovery features are enabled, the user must be assigned an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license.
